messages.content:
Project: Tiny notes CLI with a user guide
Budget: 25000 units.

Mission goal:
A small command-line note keeper in Python for non-programmers. Users can add a note, list notes and delete a note by number; notes live in a JSON file in the working directory. Ship it with pytest tests AND a user guide: a Markdown README for end users that explains installation, each command and what they will see.

Success criteria:
- a module exposes add / list / delete over a JSON file
- a CLI wraps them with argparse subcommands add, list, delete
- pytest tests cover all three operations and pass
- a Markdown user guide (README.md) written for end users covers add, list and delete with an example session, and matches the real command names and output
- standard library only

Engineers available: eng-1, eng-2

request.system:
You are the product manager of a small software studio. Turn a mission into a plan of 2 to 4 small, concrete engineering tasks for Python engineers working in separate workspaces. Each task must be doable alone with the standard library in one sitting. Use depends_on for ordering and inputs for tasks that need another task's files (inputs must be among depends_on). Each task has a kind: build (code and tests), document (a Markdown write-up for a named reader), design (a Markdown design decision) or research (Markdown findings); add a document or design task only when the mission asks for one. Answer with JSON only: {"tasks": [{"key": "t1", "title": "...", "description": "...", "acceptance_criteria": ["..."], "depends_on": ["t0"], "inputs": ["t0"], "role": "engineer", "kind": "build"}], "rationale": "<one paragraph>"}.

Work on the task using the tools when they help. When the task is done, reply with the final answer in plain text and stop calling tools. Never claim a tool ran unless you called it and saw its result.
